resources.string: Hides active VPN connection from selected apps — NetworkCapabilities, NetworkInfo, NetworkInterface, LinkProperties, /proc/net
Tap P to mark an app as a proxy-hide observer. Observer apps receive ECONNREFUSED when they try to connect to any port on 127.0.0.1 or ::1 — indistinguishable from a real closed port.
Safe for banks, госуслуги, marketplaces, non-browser apps. Chromium-based browsers use localhost for dev/PWA features — avoid adding them as observers.
Rules are re-applied on every Save. After reboot, the module restores them automatically via service.sh.
Use the checkboxes to toggle individual layers: LSPosed, Kernel, and Zygisk. Tapping the app row will toggle all available layers at once.

After saving changes: LSPosed and Kernel layers are applied instantly. Zygisk hooks are injected when the application starts, so you must force-stop and reopen the target app for Zygisk changes to take effect.
Some banking and high-security apps can detect Zygisk. If an app crashes or detects root, try disabling the Zygisk layer and use only Kernel + LSPosed instead.
Enable the Kernel bypass checkbox to force an app to ignore the VPN tunnel. Its traffic will go directly through your primary network interface (Wi-Fi or Mobile Data).
Requires the Kernel module (kmod) to be installed and active. This feature only works at the kernel level to ensure reliable routing redirection.
VPNHide Next needs root access to manage target apps. Grant root permissions to this app in your root manager (Magisk, KernelSU, etc.) and reopen the app.

Off by default — VPNHide Next keeps logcat and dmesg near-silent. You don\'t need to flip this to collect a bug report: Start recording and Collect debug log below automatically turn logging on for the duration of the capture. Use this toggle only if you want logs to be emitted continuously across the app, system_server hooks, Zygisk-hooked apps, and the kernel module (kmod logs to dmesg). Zygisk-hooked apps must be restarted for the change to take effect for them.
Records unfiltered logs from all buffers (main/system/crash/events/radio) for debugging issues that aren\'t visible in the standard checks. Start recording, reproduce the bug, then stop.
No active VPN detected. Turn on your VPN connection before running checks.
VPN is active. This app is in the target list. Results below.
Added VPNHide Next to the target list. Restart VPNHide Next (force-stop and reopen) for native-level checks to take effect — no device reboot needed.
Adding this app to target list…
Network access is disabled for this app. ioctl checks (SIOCGIFFLAGS, SIOCGIFMTU, SIOCGIFCONF) cannot run without it. Enable in Settings → Apps → VPNHide Next → Mobile data & Wi-Fi.
Installed, restart VPNHide Next to activate
Installed, did not load — try the other GKI variant
VPNHide Next was just added to its own target list. Restart VPNHide Next (force-stop and reopen) to check protection — no device reboot needed.
No active VPN. Turn on VPN to check protection status.
No active VPN. Turn it on, then tap Retry to run the protection checks. Results are cached until VPNHide Next is restarted — no need to re-run later in the same session.
\"%1$s\" in the kernel version is the GKI Kernel Module Interface tag — it identifies the kernel\'s binary interface to modules, not your Android OS release.
Kernel module is recommended. Your kernel\'s GKI branch isn\'t identifiable from uname -r, so try %1$s first; if it doesn\'t load after reboot, install %2$s instead.
Kernel module is not supported for your device. Install %1$s.

Banking and payment apps detect Zygisk hooks and crash when Z is enabled for them. Leave Z off for those apps and rely on LSPosed (Java-level) hiding — native-level hiding won\'t work for them on a kernel without kmod support.

Your kernel supports the kernel module — it hooks in kernel space and is invisible to anti-tamper checks. Zygisk works too, but its hooks can be detected by banking and payment apps, so you\'d have to keep Z off for those apps individually. Install %1$s and uninstall the Zygisk module for cleaner coverage.

Kernel module and Zygisk are both active, covering the same native paths. Kmod is invisible to anti-tamper, Zygisk isn\'t — so every time you add a banking or payment app as a target, you have to remember to leave Z off for it. Uninstall the Zygisk module to remove that per-app footgun; kmod keeps the coverage.
Debug logging is enabled. VPNHide Next is writing verbose lines to logcat that anyone with root can read. Turn it off in Diagnostics after you\'ve finished collecting a bug report.

SELinux is Permissive. Six detection vectors VPNHide Next relies on the kernel to block (RTM_GETROUTE, /proc/net/{tcp,udp,dev,fib_trie}, /sys/class/net) are reachable to target apps. Run `setenforce 1` and investigate what disabled it.
No native module installed. Install kmod or zygisk for full protection.
LSPosed/Vector is not installed. Install it and enable the VPNHide Next module for System Framework.
LSPosed is configured correctly, but its hooks are not active yet. Reboot the device to activate them.
Failed to read LSPosed/Vector configuration. Reopen LSPosed/Vector, verify that VPNHide Next is enabled there, and then reopen VPNHide Next.
VPNHide Next is present in LSPosed/Vector, but the module is disabled. Enable VPNHide Next in LSPosed/Vector and keep System Framework in its scope.
VPNHide Next is enabled in LSPosed/Vector, but System Framework is missing from its scope. Add System Framework to the VPNHide Next scope in LSPosed/Vector.
VPNHide Next should stay scoped only to System Framework in LSPosed/Vector. Remove these apps from the VPNHide Next scope: %1$s. Use Protection → Tun in VPNHide Next for filtering instead.

AOSP field rename detected on Android SDK %2$s: %1$s. Java-layer protection is degraded for the affected hooks (they were skipped at install time to avoid logcat-spam from per-call NoSuchFieldError). Please file an issue at github.com/okhsunrog/vpnhide/issues with this list so the hooks can be updated for your Android version.
No target apps configured. Go to Protection → Tun to select apps.
LSPosed module version mismatch: running %1$s, installed %2$s. Reboot the device to apply the update.
Kernel module version %1$s is older than app version %2$s. Open KernelSU/Magisk → Modules to update.
Zygisk version %1$s is older than app version %2$s. Open KernelSU/Magisk → Modules to update.
Kernel module version %1$s is newer than app version %2$s. Update the VPNHide Next app.
Zygisk version %1$s is newer than app version %2$s. Update the VPNHide Next app.
Kernel module version mismatch: module %1$s, app %2$s. Open KernelSU/Magisk → Modules to update the module.
Zygisk version mismatch: module %1$s, app %2$s. Open KernelSU/Magisk → Modules to update the module.
Wrong kernel module variant: installed %1$s, your kernel needs %2$s. Uninstall the current kmod and install %3$s from the latest release.
Kernel module is installed but not loading, and the zip doesn\'t identify which GKI variant it was built for. Reinstall %1$s from the latest release to make sure it matches your kernel.
Kernel module %1$s failed to load this boot. Your kernel\'s GKI branch isn\'t identifiable from uname -r, so install %2$s instead.
Kernel module failed to load. insmod error: %1$s. Use Diagnostics → Collect debug log to attach the full boot-time insmod output to a bug report.
Your kernel (%1$s) has no matching vpnhide-kmod variant. Uninstall the kmod module and install %2$s instead.
Your kernel was built without CONFIG_KRETPROBES. The VPNHide Next kernel module cannot work on this kernel. Uninstall kmod and use vpnhide-zygisk.zip instead.
